question.problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-2y=10\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

has the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{2x}+B{e}^{-x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.
question.worked_solution:
The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $10\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ So we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x,
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x} & =-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =-\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation:

$$
(-\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x)-(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡x)-2(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x)=10\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(-3\alpha -\beta )\operatorname{cos}⁡x+(\alpha -3\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡x=10\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}-3\alpha -\beta =10\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\ \alpha -3\beta =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-3$ and $\beta =-1.$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-3\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$
